title: IRL Black Friday was a horrifying spectacle. I miss it so much | Dave Schilling
summary: The days of coming to blows over a Furby before dawn are over. It was scary, but at least it was real Congratulations. You’re alive. And for that, I applaud you. You didn’t choke on a particularly large piece of pie or fall into a ditch on your post-Thanksgiving-meal walk. Thanksgiving is one of the more hazardous holidays on the American calendar, with all the binge eating, binge drinking and binge shopping. Continue reading...

title: Can Borussia Dortmund finally end their title wait? Three big questions for Bundesliga leaders
summary: Niko Kovac’s team lead the way and, with Bayern Munich wounded, have a golden chance to be German champions for the first time in 15 years Borussia Dortmund’s dreams have a habit of becoming nightmares, like when they somehow handed Bayern Munich the Bundesliga title on the final day of the 2022-23 season. Or when an 89th-minute Arjen Robben goal won the 2013 Champions League final for the same opponents. Whenever Dortmund suffer heartbreak, it usually involves Bayern. As things stand, however, Niko Kovac’s side hold a two-point lead over Bayern at the top of the Bundesliga. Both teams are unbeaten, but Dortmund may be the more stable of the two at the moment, especially with Harry Kane expected to miss several months through injury. Continue reading...

title: Trump Medicaid cuts will hit the most vulnerable Americans, officials say
summary: In Kentucky, one of America’s unhealthiest states, denial of healthcare and potential closure of hospitals may affect 250,000 people The coalfields of eastern Kentucky fueled America’s economic rise in the early 20th century. But the state has since found itself left behind. A lack of investments in rural regions has triggered health and socioeconomic issues that have lingered for generations. Today, Kentucky faces the third-highest cancer and third-highest drug overdose death rate in the country and is one of the top five worst-affected states in several other health metrics. It has come to rely heavily on federal healthcare assistance, with about 1.4 million people in Kentucky receiving Medicaid support. Continue reading...

title: Bills, Eagles and Bears pull off last-gasp wins in trio of Thanksgiving thrillers
summary: Bass hits from 57 yards at the gun to lift Buffalo Elliott’s 59-yarder caps Eagles’ 21-point comeback Bears take NFC North lead on Odunze’s late catch After sharing top billing, Buffalo’s Josh Allen and Kansas City’s Patrick Mahomes proved no match for the elements in the latest showdown of two of the NFL’s best quarterbacks. With both offense’s failing to gain traction on a rainy, windy and cold Thursday night, the Bills improved their AFC-leading record to 10-1 by slogging through a 13-10 victory over the visiting Chiefs on Tyler Bass’s 57-yard field goal as time expired. Buffalo have won seven straight and matched their best start to a season since 1991. Continue reading...

title: Lights-out Luka Dončić and contagious chemistry: are these Lakers for real?
summary: It’s early days, but after a dramatic roster overhaul and an offseason of team-bonding Dončić is playing at an MVP level and LA are looking like contenders One of the components of Luka Dončić’s shock trade from the Dallas Mavericks to the Los Angeles Lakers that caused great consternation was that he was just entering his prime as an NBA superstar. The worry was that the move could end that prime before it really even began – unceremoniously uprooting the Slovenian wunderkind from a team custom built around his strengths, fresh off a run to the NBA finals, to one who didn’t really make sense at all. Sure, the bright lights of Hollywood would elevate Dončić’s profile and usher him into a new echelon of stardom. But with Oklahoma City starting their run of dominance and rising stars around the league waiting in the wings, some believed his hopes of title contention (or even a long-elusive MVP award) had vanished. But the start to this season raises the question: what if they were wrong? Dončić is neck-and-neck with Victor Wembanyama in the MVP race, and the Lakers have the best record in the NBA at 15-3, with the Spurs and 76ers just behind at 15-4. San Antonio and their gargantuan French superstar were title and MVP favorites by a wide margin entering this season. But Dončić and the Lakers are keeping pace by pretty much every margin. Friday night’s NBA Cup showdown will be a duel with ripple effects and stakes rarely seen in the regular season, let alone in November. The two top records. The two leading MVP candidates. A basketball fan couldn’t ask for much more. Continue reading...

title: Mike Tomlin calls Steelers ‘dumpster fire’ as Brady rips Rodgers for breaking locker room sanctity
summary: Ex-coach says QB was ‘beloved’ by teammates Rodgers released after diatribe about McCarthy Mike Tomlin, who coached Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers last year, and Tom Brady, one of Rodgers’s longtime peers as an elite quarterback, ⁠weighed in Thursday on the 42-year-old’s dramatic exit from Pittsburgh this week. “I’m upset about it,” Tomlin said at half-time of NBC’s Thanksgiving night broadcast of the Kansas City Chiefs-Buffalo Bills game. “It’s a dumpster fire, and I don’t say that in a judgmental way. I’ve presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years, but it certainly is upsetting and I’m sure Steeler Nation is upset.” Continue reading...

Anna, a cashier in a southern Oregon Walmart and leader with United for Respect, who requested to remain anonymous for fear of retaliation, criticized the implementation of AI at Walmart and its effects on workers. title: Bigfoot enthusiasts hope government’s US sightings files are ‘just the beginning’ of proving the creature real
summary: The Forest Service’s work will ‘help normalize’ talk happening ‘for decades’, says ‘wood ape’ conservancy director When the Forest Service, one of the US government’s less sexy departments, quietly posted three documents to its website in mid-October, it was probably hoping to avoid a fuss. It didn’t succeed. The files were about Bigfoot, after all, and their publication sparked interest from around the globe, with Bigfoot enthusiasts hopeful that this could be a key step step in the road to proving the creature is real. title: Trump claims revised economic data shows pre-midterms figures were ‘fake’ | First Thing
summary: President calls for investigation after GDP figures were adjusted upwards, despite revisions to official economic figures being commonplace. Plus, the weird and macabre world of Victorian Christmas cards Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here Good morning. Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake” and demanded an investigation after voters roundly rejected his Republican party. In a holiday message on his Truth Social platform, the US president wished a happy Thanksgiving “to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%”. Why did Trump call the figures fake? Revisions to official economic figures are commonplace, but Trump has tried repeatedly to challenge trust in economic data that does not support his claims that a historic boom is under way in the US. “Why wasn’t the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. “This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error”. What other acerbic well-wishes did Trump offer? He wished “a very Happy Thanksgiving to all of those people that have worked so hard to bring our Country to the Radical Far Left” as well as “those who want to redistribute Property, so that all of the hardworking people that have built up, over a lifetime, a certain Wealth, will now be forced to distribute it throughout the Country, even to those who refuse to work”. Why are the ballots at the center of an ongoing dispute over the 2020 election? Some Republicans, led by Trump, claimed the election results had been rigged despite Joe Biden being certified after several recounts. Republican state officials had refused to overturn the result, despite a now-infamous phone call from Trump to pressure the Georgia secretary of state, Brad Raffensperger, to “find 11,780 votes”. Continue reading...

title: Three studies link glyphosate to cancer, contradicting claims of Trump EPA
summary: Experts say NIH research raises concerns about chemical companies’ influence on US agency’s pesticide division The US government’s top medical research agency has released three new studies linking glyphosate, the world’s most widely used pesticide and an active ingredient in Roundup, to cancer . The National Institutes of Health (NIH) findings contradicts a controversial recent Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) conclusion that the weed killer is not a carcinogen, and deals a blow to the White House, which has been closely allied with Roundup producer Bayer. The NIH’s three papers could have significant political and legal fallout. The EPA is in the process of a court-ordered re-evaluation of glyphosate’s cancer risks. The NIH findings generates new pressure for the EPA to find that the substance is linked to cancer, which would subject it to a modest increase in regulations. Continue reading...

title: Eastern US recovers from storms that snarled Thanksgiving travel as flooding continues
summary: Heavy rains and high winds downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia Skies are clearing along the US eastern seaboard, and power was being restored to hundreds of thousands of customers, whose Thanksgiving plans were disrupted by heavy rains and high winds that swept over the region Thursday. The storms snarled travel, downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia. At its peak, nearly a million customers were without power and widespread coastal flooding was reported by Poweroutage.us. Continue reading...

title: King tides batter US coasts as storms threaten Thanksgiving celebrations
summary: Heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding creating hazardous conditions for millions travelling for holiday King tides and huge waves have been battering both coasts of the US during a turbulent Thanksgiving period, with severe weather threatening millions across the country. Along the California coast, king tides caused considerable damage. In Pacifica, south of San Francisco, large waves battered the coastline on Wednesday, destroying part of a pier and sending debris into the ocean. The National Weather Service issued coastal flood warnings covering parts of the Pacific coastline and shorelines around San Francisco Bay and San Pablo Bay. Several beachfront properties in Pacifica have already experienced flooding, while authorities in Marin County temporarily issued an evacuation warning for residents of beachfront homes at Stinson Beach. Continue reading...

title: Newly released documents suggest CIA did more post-9/11 waterboarding than previously acknowledged
summary: Declassified documents appear to support belief that waterboarding was more common and may have occurred beyond two acknowledged sites Newly released documents suggest that the CIA waterboarded more detainees during the post-9/11 “war on terror” than previously acknowledged, utilizing a site north of Kabul, Afghanistan, for the practice of simulated drowning. The agency has acknowledged waterboarding three men: Abu Zubaydah, believed to be a high-ranking member of al-Qaida; Khalid Shaikh Mohammed, suspected architect of the 11 September 2001 attacks; and Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri, accused of planning the 2000 bombing of a Navy destroyer. Continue reading...

title: Thanksgiving meal in Florida leads to mass food poisoning incident
summary: Local media reported that 18 people fell ill after attending a Thanksgiving lunch at a medical center headquarters A Thanksgiving meal in Florida triggered a bout of food poisoning so bad that local emergency officials said it was a “mass casualty” event as numerous stricken diners were sent to hospital. Local media reported that 18 people at the Leon Medical Center headquarters in Doral fell ill due to possible food poisoning after attending the center’s annual Thanksgiving lunch on Wednesday.
